questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Ephemeral PR environments are a cornerstone of modern DevOps practices, enabling teams to validate changes in isolated environments without affecting production. This question assesses the candidate's understanding of Kubernetes lifecycle management, infrastructure-as-code practices, and observability in cloud-native deployments.

## Key Concepts
- PR-triggered ephemeral environments for isolated testing
- Kubernetes namespaces dynamically provisioned per PR
- Helm-based application deployments
- End-to-end smoke testing in isolated environments
- Automated teardown with policy safeguards and comprehensive logging

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  paths:
    include:
    - src/**
    - charts/**
    - azure-pipelines.yml

variables:
  PR_NUMBER: $(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
  NAMESPACE: 'pr-$(PR_NUMBER)'
  RETENTION_HOURS: 24
  AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION: 'Azure-Production'
  AKS_CLUSTER: 'aks-cluster-01'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: 'rg-aks-prod'

stages:
- stage: Provision
  displayName: 'Provision Ephemeral Environment'
  jobs:
  - job: CreateNamespace
    displayName: 'Create PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Create AKS Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing
          
          kubectl create namespace $(NAMESPACE) --dry-run=client -o yaml | \
            kubectl apply -f -
          
          kubectl label namespace $(NAMESPACE) \
            pr.number=$(PR_NUMBER) \
            pr.created=$(Build.BuildNumber) \
            environment=ephemeral --overwrite
          
          echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=NAMESPACE;isOutput=true]$(NAMESPACE)"
      name: namespaceInfo

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor log-analytics query \
            --workspace $(LOG_WORKSPACE_ID) \
            --query "['EphemeralEnvironmentCreated']" \
            --analytics-duration 1 | tee /dev/stderr

- stage: Deploy
  displayName: 'Deploy Application'
  dependsOn: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: HelmDeploy
    displayName: 'Deploy with Helm'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: HelmInstaller@1
      displayName: 'Install Helm'
      inputs:
        helmVersionToInstall: 'latest'

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Configure AKS Credentials'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing

    - task: HelmDeploy@0
      displayName: 'Deploy Helm Chart'
      inputs:
        connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        azureResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
        kubernetesCluster: '$(AKS_CLUSTER)'
        namespace: '$(NAMESPACE)'
        chartName: '$(CHART_REPO)/$(CHART_NAME)'
        chartVersion: '$(Build.BuildNumber)'
        releaseName: 'pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER)'
        overrideValues: |
          image.tag=$(Build.BuildNumber)
          ingress.hostname=$(NAMESPACE).$(DOMAIN)

- stage: Test
  displayName: 'Smoke Tests'
  dependsOn: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: SmokeTests
    displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Wait for Deployment'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl wait --for=condition=available \
            --timeout=300s \
            deployment/pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER) \
            -n $(NAMESPACE)

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc -n $(NAMESPACE) \
            -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
          
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/api/version || exit 1

- stage: Teardown
  displayName: 'Teardown Environment'
  condition: or(
    eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'),
    eq(dependencies.Provision.outputs['CreateNamespace.namespaceInfo.namespace'], '')
  )
  jobs:
  - job: DeleteNamespace
    displayName: 'Delete PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Policy Check Before Deletion'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          NAMESPACE=$(NAMESPACE)
          if [[ "$NAMESPACE" == pr-* ]]; then
            echo "Validating deletion policy for ephemeral namespace..."
            az policy assignment list \
              --scope /subscriptions/$(SUB_ID)/resourceGroups/$(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
              --query "[?displayName=='ProtectEphemeralNamespaces']" | tee /dev/stderr
          else
            echo "##vso[task.logissue type=warning]Non-PR namespace - skipping deletion"
            exit 1
          fi

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Delete Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl delete namespace $(NAMESPACE) --wait=true
          
          echo "Namespace $(NAMESPACE) deleted successfully"

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log Deletion to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor metrics alert create \
            --name "namespace-deleted-$(NAMESPACE)" \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --description "Ephemeral namespace $(NAMESPACE) has been deleted"

resources:
  webhooks:
  - webhook: PRClosed
    connectionType: 'azureDevOps'
    project: '$(System.TeamProject)'
    pipeline: '$(Build.DefinitionName)'

schedules:
- cron: '0 0 * * *'
  displayName: 'Daily Cleanup'
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  always: true
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Namespace Creation**: Dynamically creates pr-${PR_NUMBER} namespace with metadata labels for tracking
2. **Helm Deployment**: Uses HelmDeploy@0 task with Azure Resource Manager connection for secure deployment
3. **Smoke Testing**: Validates application health and API endpoints post-deployment
4. **Policy Protection**: Validates namespace pattern before deletion to prevent accidental removal of non-prod environments
5. **Azure Monitor Logging**: All operations are logged for audit and troubleshooting
6. **Scheduled Cleanup**: Cron job ensures stale environments are removed after 24 hours
7. **Webhook Integration**: Triggers cleanup when PR is merged or closed

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question validates the ability to combine per-tenant isolation, cost governance, and centralized telemetry management within a single automated pipeline with built-in rollback capabilities.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant resource scoping with dedicated resource groups, App Configuration, and Key Vault
- Tenant-specific App Service slots with isolated configuration
- Real-time cost forecasting and governance via Azure Cost Management
- Telemetry segregation using tenant-scoped Log Analytics workspaces
- Drift detection and automated rollback strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Azure DevOps YAML Pipeline for Multi-Tenant Onboarding
trigger: none
pr: none

parameters:
  - name: tenantId
    type: string
  - name: tenantName
    type: string
  - name: costThresholdUSD
    type: number
    default: 500

stages:
  - stage: PreValidation
    jobs:
      - job: CostForecastGate
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: CheckCostForecast
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                # Query Cost Management for 30-day forecast
                COST=$(az cost management query \
                  --scope /subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID \
                  --query "properties[0].columns[?(@.name=='Cost')].rows[0]" \
                  --timeframe ThisMonth \
                  --dataset-name CurrentMonth \
                  -o tsv)
                
                PROJECTED=$(( COST * 30 / $(date +%d) ))
                
                if [ $PROJECTED -gt ${{ parameters.costThresholdUSD }} ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Projected cost \$$PROJECTED exceeds threshold \$${{ parameters.costThresholdUSD }}"
                  exit 1
                fi

  - stage: ProvisionResources
    dependsOn: PreValidation
    jobs:
      - job: CreateTenantResources
        steps:
          - task: AzureResourceGroupDeployment@3
            name: ProvisionRG
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              resourceGroupName: 'rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              location: 'East US'
              templateLocation: 'Inline'
              mode: 'Incremental'

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: ProvisionAppConfig
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az appconfig create \
                  --name "appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: ProvisionKeyVault
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az keyvault create \
                  --name "kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: CreateLogAnalytics
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor log-analytics workspace create \
                  --workspace-name "la-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

  - stage: DeployAppService
    dependsOn: ProvisionResources
    jobs:
      - job: DeploySlot
        steps:
          - task: AzureAppServiceSettings@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              appName: 'saas-api-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              slotName: 'staging'
              appSettings: |
                TENANT_ID=${{ parameters.tenantId }}
                APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT=https://appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}.azconfig.io
                KEY_VAULT_URI=https://kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}.vault.azure.net/
                LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_ID=$(az monitor log-analytics workspace show --workspace-name la-${{ parameters.tenantName }} --resource-group rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }} --query customerId -o tsv)

          - task: AzureAppServiceManage@0
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              Action: 'Swap Slots'
              WebAppName: 'saas-api-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              SourceSlot: 'staging'

  - stage: ValidateAndMonitor
    dependsOn: DeployAppService
    jobs:
      - job: HealthCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: VerifyTenantAccess
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                # Verify Key Vault access policy and App Configuration keys
                az keyvault secret list --vault-name "kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" | jq 'length'
                az appconfig kv list --name "appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" | jq 'length'

          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            inputs:
              targetPath: '$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)'
              artifact: 'tenant-config-${{ parameters.tenantId }}'
```

## Testing Strategy
1. **Unit Testing**: Validate ARM template outputs and Bicep configurations with Az CLI dry-run
2. **Integration Testing**: Verify cost gate logic with mocked Cost Management responses
3. **E2E Testing**: Spin up a test tenant and validate resource provisioning, slot deployment, and telemetry routing
4. **Chaos Testing**: Simulate cost threshold exceeded scenarios to confirm pipeline blocks deployment
5. **Compliance Testing**: Ensure tenant resources are properly isolated with RBAC validation

## Why This Is Asked
Monorepo PR validation must balance speed with coverage by testing only affected packages while maintaining quality gates.

## Key Concepts
- Path-based triggers and changed files detection
- npm workspaces and selective package testing
- Dynamic matrix strategy and conditional job execution
- Per-package artifact publishing

## Code Example

```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml
trigger:
  none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - '*'

variables:
  - name: changedPackages
    value: ''
  - name: workspaceRoot
    value: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)'

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  jobs:
  - job: GetChangedPackages
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '18.x'
    - script: |
        # Get changed files and extract package names
        changedFiles=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)
        packages=$(echo "$changedFiles" | grep -E '^packages/[^/]+/' | cut -d'/' -f2 | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedPackages;isOutput=true]$packages"
      name: detectChanges
    - script: |
        echo "Changed packages: $(detectChanges.changedPackages)"

- stage: TestAndBuild
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: ne(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['GetChangedPackages.detectChanges.changedPackages'], '')
  jobs:
  - job: TestPackages
    strategy:
      matrix:
        $[ each(package in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['GetChangedPackages.detectChanges.changedPackages'], ' ')) ]:
          ${{ package }}:
            packageName: ${{ package }}
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '18.x'
    - script: |
        # Install dependencies for the specific package
        npm ci --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Install package dependencies'
    - script: |
        # Run tests for the specific package
        npm test --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Run package tests'
    - script: |
        # Build the package
        npm run build --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Build package'
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs:
        PathtoPublish: 'packages/$(packageName)/dist'
        ArtifactName: '$(packageName)-artifact'
      displayName: 'Publish package artifact'
      condition: succeeded()

- stage: QualityGate
  dependsOn: TestAndBuild
  jobs:
  - job: ValidateAllTests
    steps:
    - script: |
        echo "All changed packages have been tested and built successfully"
        echo "PR validation passed - ready for merge"
      displayName: 'Quality gate validation'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the candidate's ability to design end-to-end tenant onboarding, isolation, governance, and observability in Azure DevOps at production scale.

## Key Concepts
- Parameterized YAML templates and conditional deployment
- Per-tenant resource isolation: Resource Group, App Service plan, deployment slot
- App Configuration and Key Vault integration
- Database seeding and tenant-specific tests in isolated environments
- Policy gates and drift detection
- Rollback strategy and per-tenant auditing to Azure Monitor

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none

parameters:
  - name: tenantId
    type: string
    displayName: 'Tenant ID'
  - name: tenantDomain
    type: string
    displayName: 'Tenant Domain'

variables:
  azureServiceConnection: 'azure-spn'
  subscriptionId: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID)'
  resourceGroupName: 'rg-$(tenantId)'
  appServicePlanName: 'asp-$(tenantId)'
  appServiceName: 'api-$(tenantId)'
  appConfigName: 'appconfig-$(tenantId)'
  keyVaultName: 'kv-shared-01'
  databaseServerName: 'sql-$(tenantId)'
  databaseName: 'db-$(tenantId)'

stages:
  - stage: Provision
    displayName: 'Provision Tenant Resources'
    jobs:
      - job: ProvisionResources
        displayName: 'Provision Infrastructure'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create Resource Group'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az group create --name $(resourceGroupName) --location eastus
                az configure --defaults group=$(resourceGroupName)

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create App Service Plan'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az appservice plan create --name $(appServicePlanName) --sku S1 --is-linux

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create App Service with Deployment Slot'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az webapp create --name $(appServiceName) --plan $(appServicePlanName) --runtime 'NODE|18-lts'
                az webapp deployment slot create --name $(appServiceName) --slot staging

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create SQL Database'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az sql server create --name $(databaseServerName) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --location eastus
                az sql db create --name $(databaseName) --server $(databaseServerName) --service-tier Basic

  - stage: Configure
    displayName: 'Configure Tenant'
    dependsOn: Provision
    jobs:
      - job: LoadConfiguration
        displayName: 'Load Settings and Secrets'
        steps:
          - task: AzureKeyVault@2
            displayName: 'Fetch Tenant Secrets'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              KeyVaultName: $(keyVaultName)
              SecretsFilter: '*'
              RunAsPreJob: false

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Configure App Settings'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az webapp config appsettings set --name $(appServiceName) --slot staging --settings \
                  TENANT_ID=$(tenantId) \
                  TENANT_DOMAIN=$(tenantDomain) \
                  DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING='Server=tcp:$(databaseServerName).database.windows.net,1433;Database=$(databaseName);User ID=$(keyVaultTenantUser);Password=$(keyVaultTenantPassword);Encrypt=true;'

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Seed Database'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                sqlcmd -S $(databaseServerName).database.windows.net -d $(databaseName) -U $(keyVaultTenantUser) -P $(keyVaultTenantPassword) -i seed-tenant.sql

  - stage: Deploy
    displayName: 'Deploy to Staging'
    dependsOn: Configure
    jobs:
      - job: DeployApplication
        displayName: 'Deploy to Staging Slot'
        steps:
          - task: AzureWebApp@1
            displayName: 'Deploy to Staging Slot'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              appType: 'webApp'
              appName: $(appServiceName)
              deployToSlotOrASE: true
              resourceGroupName: $(resourceGroupName)
              slotName: 'staging'

  - stage: Test
    displayName: 'Run Tests'
    dependsOn: Deploy
    jobs:
      - job: RunTests
        displayName: 'Execute Tenant Tests'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Run Unit Tests'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                npm test -- --tenantId=$(tenantId) --environment=staging

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Run Integration Tests'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                npm run test:integration -- --tenantId=$(tenantId) --environment=staging

  - stage: GateAndPolicy
    displayName: 'Policy Gates & Drift Check'
    dependsOn: Test
    jobs:
      - job: PolicyCheck
        displayName: 'Verify Policy Compliance'
        steps:
          - task: AzurePolicy@0
            displayName: 'Check Azure Policy Compliance'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              resourceGroupName: $(resourceGroupName)
              definitionId: '/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions/...' 

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Drift Detection'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az deployment group show --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --name initial-deployment
                # Compare current state with desired state

  - stage: Promote
    displayName: 'Promote to Production'
    dependsOn: GateAndPolicy
    condition: succeeded()
    jobs:
      - job: SwapSlots
        displayName: 'Swap Staging to Production'
        steps:
          - task: AzureAppServiceManage@0
            displayName: 'Swap Staging to Production'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              Action: 'Swap Slots'
              WebAppName: $(appServiceName)
              ResourceGroupName: $(resourceGroupName)
              SourceSlot: 'staging'

  - stage: Audit
    displayName: 'Audit & Logging'
    dependsOn: Promote
    jobs:
      - job: LogAuditTrail
        displayName: 'Send Audit Logs to Azure Monitor'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Log Tenant Onboarding'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor app-insights trace show \
                  --location eastus \
                  --query "[?operationName == 'tenant-onboarding']"

                # Send custom event
                az monitor app-insights events show --app $(appInsightsName) --type customEvents
```

This YAML pipeline demonstrates a complete tenant onboarding workflow with infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, testing, policy enforcement, and production deployment with full audit logging capabilities.
